label: Title men-at-arms regiment
summary: Each men-at-arms regiment belonging to the title.
details: Works on a title. The items are regiments, not characters. Vanilla only uses the `any_` form: three times as a plain check with nothing inside, and twice with `count >= 1`.

label: Neighboring or overseas county
summary: Each county that borders the title, including counties reached across water.
details: Works on a title and gives titles. The neighbors are found by looking through the de jure lieges (the titles each title belongs to by the map's own hierarchy). Vanilla uses it to check who holds the neighboring counties and to set the culture of neighbors.

label: Neighboring or overseas duchy
summary: Each duchy that borders the title, including duchies reached across water.
details: Works on a title and gives titles. The neighbors are found by looking through the de jure lieges. Vanilla mostly uses it to test whether a given duchy is among the neighbors, and to pick a random neighboring duchy as a destination.

label: Neighboring or overseas empire
summary: Each empire that borders the title, including empires reached across water.
details: Works on a title and gives titles. The neighbors are found by looking through the de jure lieges. Vanilla uses it to check whether a given empire is among the neighbors, and to pick a random neighboring empire.

label: Neighboring or overseas kingdom
summary: Each kingdom that borders the title, including kingdoms reached across water.
details: Works on a title and gives titles. The neighbors are found by looking through the de jure lieges. Vanilla uses it to check whether a given kingdom is among the neighbors, and to pick a random neighboring kingdom (with a limit and a weight) and save it for later.

label: Neighboring county
summary: Each county that borders the title.
details: Works on a title and gives titles. The neighbors are found by looking through the de jure lieges. The game's text mentions water crossings only for the "or overseas" version, so this one presumably leaves them out. Vanilla uses it to compare the holders' top lieges and to order neighbors by military strength.

label: Neighboring duchy
summary: Each duchy that borders the title.
details: Works on a title and gives titles. The neighbors are found by looking through the de jure lieges. The game's text mentions water crossings only for the "or overseas" version, so this one presumably leaves them out. Vanilla uses it to collect neighbors into a list and to test whether a duchy is among them.

label: Neighboring empire
summary: Each empire that borders the title.
details: Works on a title and gives titles. The neighbors are found by looking through the de jure lieges. The game's text mentions water crossings only for the "or overseas" version, so this one presumably leaves them out. Vanilla uses it exactly once, in a check that involves the title `h_china`.

label: Neighboring kingdom
summary: Each kingdom that borders the title.
details: Works on a title and gives titles. The neighbors are found by looking through the de jure lieges. The game's text mentions water crossings only for the "or overseas" version, so this one presumably leaves them out. Vanilla uses it to test whether a given kingdom is among the neighbors.

label: Top realm border county
summary: Each county of the character's realm that lies on the edge where it meets a different neighboring top realm.
details: Works on a character and gives county titles. Vanilla uses it to gather border counties into a list and to pick a random border county and save it as a contested or own county.

label: Tradition
summary: Each cultural tradition of the culture.
details: Works on a culture and gives its traditions. Vanilla uses `random_tradition` a lot to pick a few traditions to consider, and `any_tradition` to check traditions by category (realm, combat, societal, ritual, regional).

label: Trait
summary: Every trait that exists in the game.
details: The game names no scope it must run in, so it works anywhere. The items are the trait definitions, not characters that have the trait. Vanilla uses `random_trait` with a limit to pick one trait and save it for later.

label: Trait in category
summary: Every trait that belongs to the given trait category.
details: The game names no scope it must run in, so it works anywhere. The items are the trait definitions, not characters. Vanilla uses categories such as `personality`, `education` and `lifestyle`.

fields.name: category
fields.text: Which trait category to go through.
fields.values: a trait category, for example personality, education, lifestyle, fame or health

label: Traveling family member
summary: Each character who should travel along with the character, including the character themself.
details: Works on a character. The game's text names moving between courts as one case where such a group travels together. Vanilla uses it to move the whole group to a pool or into a court.

label: Tributary
summary: Each character who is a tributary of the character.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla uses it to end tributary relations (`end_tributary = yes`), to collect tributaries into lists, and to check their government or title rank.

label: Truce holder
summary: Each character who has a truce on the character.
details: Works on a character. The game's text does not spell out which side the truce protects. Vanilla uses it to find the strongest of them (by military strength) and to check whether a given character is among them.

label: Truce target
summary: Each character the character has a truce on.
details: Works on a character. It is the counterpart of the truce holder list, with the two roles swapped. Vanilla uses it to cancel a truce one way and to find the strongest of them (by military strength).

label: Unassigned taxpayer
summary: Each unassigned taxpayer of the character.
details: Works on a character. The game documents only this one line, and vanilla never uses it, so what makes a taxpayer unassigned is not stated.

label: Undesired tenet
summary: Each core tenet of the character's rite that the character would most like to swap out, worst first.
details: Works on a character and gives tenets. The order follows how much each tenet lowers the character's starting fulfillment, worst to best. Without options, tenets that help fulfillment are included too. The game's own text contains an example named `every_undesired_core_tenet`, which does not match this key. Vanilla's `any_` uses combine `only_negative = yes`, `known_tenets = yes`, `threshold = -1` and `selection_count = 97`.

fields.name: only_negative
fields.text: Leaves out tenets that benefit the character's starting fulfillment.

fields.name: threshold
fields.text: Only keeps tenets whose fulfillment change is this value or lower. Works only together with only_negative = yes.

fields.name: selection_count
fields.text: Limits the list to the first N worst tenets. The core tenet cap of the game still applies.

fields.name: known_tenets
fields.text: Looks at all tenets the character knows, not only the current core tenets of their rite.

label: Unspent known secret
summary: Each secret the character knows about that has not been used up yet.
details: Works on a character and gives secrets. What counts as spent is not stated: the game's text says only "unspent", and vanilla never uses this list. Reading it as "not yet used" is an inference from the name.

label: Vassal
summary: Each direct vassal of the character.
details: Only direct vassals, not the vassals' own vassals. For the whole chain use the vassal-or-below list. Vanilla often filters by vassal stance (zealot, courtly, glory hound, parochial, minority). It is used about two thousand times across its `every_`, `random_`, `ordered_` and `any_` forms.

fields.name: vassal_stance
fields.text: Only keeps vassals with this stance. Given in the game's text for the `any_` form.
fields.values: a vassal stance, for example parochial, zealot, courtly, glory_hound or minority

label: Vassal contract
summary: Every vassal contract type that exists in the game.
details: The game names no scope it must run in. The items are the contract definitions, not the contracts between particular characters. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Vassal or below
summary: Each vassal of the character, direct or further down the chain.
details: This includes the vassals of vassals and so on, unlike the plain vassal list, which has only direct vassals. Vanilla also filters it by vassal stance.

fields.name: vassal_stance
fields.text: Only keeps vassals with this stance. Given in the game's text for the `any_` form.
fields.values: a vassal stance, for example parochial, zealot, courtly, glory_hound or minority

label: Visited location
summary: Each province a travel plan has already arrived at.
details: Works on a travel plan and gives provinces. Vanilla uses `ordered_visited_location` with `position = end` and saves the result as the last visited location, and `random_visited_location` to pick any visited province.

label: War ally
summary: Each character who is a direct war ally of the character.
details: Works on a character. The game's text says "direct", so allies of allies are presumably not included. Vanilla uses it mostly to check who is an ally, and once to send an interface message to all of them.

label: War attacker
summary: Each character on the attacking side of the war.
details: Works on a war and gives characters. Vanilla uses it to collect attackers into lists, to check whether someone is among them, and to give achievement flags.

label: War defender
summary: Each character on the defending side of the war.
details: Works on a war and gives characters. Vanilla uses it to collect defenders into lists, to check whether someone is among them, and to give achievement flags.

label: War enemy
summary: Each character the character is directly at war against.
details: Works on a character. The game's text says "direct", so only direct enemies are meant. Vanilla uses it to find the strongest enemy, to pick a random one, and to send messages to all of them.

label: War participant
summary: Each character who takes part in the war.
details: Works on a war and gives characters. Compare the war attacker and war defender lists, which cover one side each. Vanilla uses it, for example, to remove contract-assistance variables from the participants.

label: Held hostage
summary: Each hostage the character holds as their warden.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla uses it to collect suitable children among the hostages into lists and to pick a random one by their home court or age.
